description: An enthusiastic team of 6 high schoolers who want to build engaging products that change the world!
summary:
Lunaris360 puts you on the surface of the Moon. Pick any landing site, drop into a first-person view, and watch the Sun crawl along the horizon and Earth hang in the sky exactly where they would at that place and time. Behind the view is one of the largest collections of lunar planning data in a single place: 43 curated landing sites, 169 high-resolution terrain tiles, nearly 50 MB of processed NASA elevation, illumination, temperature and mineral data, and JPL Horizons positions for the Sun and Earth through 2030.

An AI mission assistant works alongside you. Ask it which site gets the most sunlight, when Earth drops below the horizon, or how to lay out a base, and it answers from the real data. It can also place habitats, solar arrays, comms towers and rovers on the terrain for you, checking slope and spacing the same way a planner would.

Today, planners have to jump between LROC QuickMap, Moon Trek and JPL Horizons, three powerful tools that were never designed to work together. Lunaris360 brings them into one interactive platform, checked against every Apollo landing. Guided Mission teaches anyone why landing sites matter, and Open Exploration gives experts the tools to plan the next one, from science landers to fusion plants, data centers and staging points for Mars.
details:
Lunaris360 turns lunar mission planning into something you can see, explore and test. It combines NASA data, 3D visualization and an AI assistant to show why choosing a landing site is one of the hardest decisions in lunar exploration.

The platform has two experiences. Guided Mission walks the public through three chapters: the first crewed landing, a robotic explorer and a long-term lunar base. Each one uses real missions and decisions with real consequences. Open Exploration is built for experts and mission planners. They can spin a Moon globe layered with Moon Trek imagery and LROC data, compare sites on elevation, slope, temperature, water-ice potential and mineral composition, plot launch windows and transfer trajectories, and read graphs of sunlight and Earth visibility over days or a full year. Then they can drop into a first-person surface view and stand at the site itself.

The integrated AI assistant, built on Google Gemini through Firebase, answers questions using the same data as the rest of the app. It can also build a base layout on the surface, placing habitat domes, inflatable modules, solar arrays, comms towers and rovers, and it rejects placements on slopes or spots that are too crowded.

The science is real and verified. Sun and Earth positions come from JPL Horizons. Terrain and horizon calculations use NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data and NASA Goddard’s high-resolution polar elevation models. Illumination, shadowed-crater and temperature layers come from LRO’s LROC and Diviner instruments. We checked our calculations against the recorded sun angle at all six Apollo landings, and every one matched within 0.06°. Heritage zones from NASA’s 2011 guidelines for protecting Apollo landing sites are built in so planners avoid historic sites.

Throughout development, we focused on accuracy, usability and the different needs of researchers, educators, companies and the public. Lunaris360 makes the Moon’s most complex data clear enough to act on, for anyone planning humanity’s next step there.
